nodes.description: C4 is cleaved by MASP-2 alone among the MASPs, so loss of MASP-2 function removes the lectin pathway's route to the C3 convertase C4b2a and abolishes lectin-pathway activity outright. This is a stronger molecular lesion than a recognition-molecule deficiency such as ficolin-3 deficiency, where the remaining recognition molecules still reach the same enzyme. The classical and alternative pathways are unaffected.

nodes.description: MASP-2 circulates in complexes with the recognition molecules of the lectin pathway and is activated when one of them binds a microbial or altered-self surface. The p.D120G substitution falls in the region that mediates that association: recombinant D120G MASP-2 does not bind mannose-binding lectin, so the enzyme is never recruited to a recognised surface. The variant is found in Europeans and in Inuit from West Greenland and not in the other populations surveyed.

nodes.description: Recurrent pyogenic infection is the phenotype the primary-immunodeficiency classification of MASP-2 deficiency asserts, and the 2003 index patient presented with it. No frequency is tagged, and that is the point of this record: the eleven published homozygous patients have no shared presentation, nine published homozygotes are healthy, and a study powered to find them identified no homozygote among 1495 adults with community-acquired pneumonia or 103 children with invasive pneumococcal disease. Both readings are curated below.

nodes.description: With no lectin-pathway C4 cleavage, complement opsonins are not deposited by this route, and complement-receptor-mediated uptake of the organism by neutrophils and macrophages is correspondingly reduced. This is the mechanism the classification of MASP-2 deficiency as a primary immunodeficiency assumes. Whether it produces measurable susceptibility in people is the entry's central open question: the classical and alternative pathways still opsonise, and the evidence below runs both ways.
